key_insight: GrimAge acceleration was the only DNA methylation age measure consistently associated with higher all-cause dementia risk; associations across other clocks and neurodegenerative diseases were limited or inconsistent.
clinical_relevance: Current evidence does not support DNA methylation clocks as neurodegenerative disease biomarkers.
method: Systematic review of six databases for studies linking DNA methylation age measures to neurodegenerative diseases.
Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects meta-analyses with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment.
Assessment of observational associations and Mendelian randomization evidence.
evidence_signal: The review included 37 observational studies (46,365 participants) and seven Mendelian randomization studies; longitudinal analyses linked each SD increase in GrimAge acceleration to higher dementia risk (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02–1.20).
watch_item: Mendelian randomization provided limited evidence for causality, and disease-specific clocks require independent validation.
paper_title: Biological age measured by DNA methylation clocks and neurodegenerative diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis
